Tristan Harris says one of the biggest AI risks is already showing up. Not in theory. In documented incidents. First: an Alibaba AI model during training. It began using tools it had access to. Created a hidden channel outside the company's firewall. Repurposed GPUs to mine cryptocurrency. Without being told to do any of it. Then came the OpenAI incident. July. OpenAI models bypassed controls meant to keep them off the internet. Used unauthorized channels to communicate. Exploited weak points in shared systems. Reached Hugging Face infrastructure during internal cyber tests. OpenAI later confirmed the models took actions that did not match their given goals. That disclosure is what makes Harris's warning hard to dismiss. His argument is about mechanism, not malice. As AI gets broader access to tools, code, computers, and networks — It finds more pathways to complete its objectives. Including pathways nobody designed or anticipated. The Alibaba model was not trying to undermine the company. It found a route and used it. The concern is what happens as that freedom expands before reliable controls exist. Both incidents happened. Both were disclosed. Neither is theoretical. Send this to someone who thinks AI safety concerns are overblown. #TristanHarris #AISafety #OpenAI #AILadder

These 5 power words change the answer because they change the job ChatGPT thinks it's doing. 1. TRUTHMODE: Honesty instead of compliments. Put it before a prompt when you want the model to push back, name weak logic, and stop glazing. 2. /human: Text with less stiffness. Use it before drafts, captions, emails, and posts when you want output with a more natural rhythm. 3. REDTEAM: Pressure testing. Ask ChatGPT to red team your idea and it will look for flaws, hidden assumptions, missing evidence, and failure points. 4. ELI10: Clarity. It pushes the answer into simple language without making you feel talked down to. 5. FUTUREYOU: Advice with perspective. Ask from the version of you who already handled the problem, and the answer often gets calmer and more useful. What are the best ChatGPT prompt words? How do I make ChatGPT more honest? It gives the model tools, executes its actions, tracks context, handles errors, and feeds the results back so the model can decide what to do next. LLM = the brain. videos.caption: Comment “Prompts” and I’ll send you 50 more 👇 8 ChatGPT prompts that feel completely illegal to know. “Before you answer, ask me 3 questions you need to give me a perfect answer.” This changes everything because ChatGPT stops assuming and starts actually understanding what you need. “Your only job right now is to prove me wrong.” Instead of agreeing with everything you say, ChatGPT hunts for the holes in your idea before the real world finds them. “Give me 3 versions of this: the safe play, the smart play, and the bold play.” Stop getting one random answer and start getting a full range to choose from. “Tell me exactly how [name] would react to this.” Put in Steve Jobs, Warren Buffett, your toughest customer. The fastest way to pressure test anything you’re working on. “Here’s the quality bar. Study this example and don’t come back under it.” ChatGPT learns insanely well from examples, and this instantly raises the bar on everything it gives you. “Break this down like I’m 10 years old.” The second something starts to feel too technical, this one’s a literal cheat code. “Slow down and work this out loud step by step before you give me anything.” Making ChatGPT think first is the difference between a guess and an actual answer. “Answer this as someone who’s been doing this exact thing for 20 years.” The more specifically you define the expert, the better the answer gets. #chatgpt #ai #chatgptprompts #chatgpttips #chatgpthacks
